objectives.description: Recognize the closure condition that defines an ideal.

sources.citation: Original prerequisite check prepared for the Axiora design fixture.
sources.rights: No third-party text reproduced; distribution license not yet selected.

select-condition.prompt_md: Which condition is part of the definition of an ideal $I$ in a ring $R$?

options.text_md: For every $a \in I$ and $r \in R$, $ra \in I$.
Whenever $ab \in I$, one of $a$ or $b$ lies in $I$.

feedback.correct_md: Correct. Closure under multiplication by ring elements is part of the ideal condition.
feedback.incorrect_md: The second condition is the additional defining property of a prime ideal.

recall.content_md: An ideal is an additive subgroup closed under multiplication by arbitrary elements of the ring. Primality adds the condition that $ab \in I$ forces $a \in I$ or $b \in I$.

remediate.content_md: Keep the two conditions separate: ideal closure is required for every ring element multiplying an element of $I$; the product condition distinguishes prime ideals among ideals.

finish.summary_md: You reviewed the ideal condition used by the next unit. This short check is practice, not evidence of proof skill.
